nodes.Name: Error
nodes.DocComment:
An Error describes a failure to parse a regular expression
and gives the offending expression.

nodes.Name: ErrorCode
nodes.DocComment: An ErrorCode describes a failure to parse a regular expression.

nodes.Name: Flags
nodes.DocComment: Flags control the behavior of the parser and record information about regexp context.

nodes.Name: opLeftParen
nodes.DocComment: Pseudo-ops for parsing stack.

nodes.Name: opVerticalBar
nodes.DocComment: Pseudo-ops for parsing stack.

nodes.Name: maxHeight
nodes.DocComment:
maxHeight is the maximum height of a regexp parse tree.
It is somewhat arbitrarily chosen, but the idea is to be large enough
that no one will actually hit in real use but at the same time small enough
that recursion on the Regexp tree will not hit the 1GB Go stack limit.
The maximum amount of stack for a single recursive frame is probably
closer to 1kB, so this could potentially be raised, but it seems unlikely
that people have regexps nested even this deeply.
We ran a test on Google's C++ code base and turned up only
a single use case with depth > 100; it had depth 128.
Using depth 1000 should be plenty of margin.
As an optimization, we don't even bother calculating heights
until we've allocated at least maxHeight Regexp structures.

nodes.Name: maxSize
nodes.DocComment:
maxSize is the maximum size of a compiled regexp in Insts.
It too is somewhat arbitrarily chosen, but the idea is to be large enough
to allow significant regexps while at the same time small enough that
the compiled form will not take up too much memory.
128 MB is enough for a 3.3 million Inst structures, which roughly
corresponds to a 3.3 MB regexp.

nodes.Name: instSize
nodes.DocComment:
maxSize is the maximum size of a compiled regexp in Insts.
It too is somewhat arbitrarily chosen, but the idea is to be large enough
to allow significant regexps while at the same time small enough that
the compiled form will not take up too much memory.
128 MB is enough for a 3.3 million Inst structures, which roughly
corresponds to a 3.3 MB regexp.

nodes.Name: maxRunes
nodes.DocComment:
maxRunes is the maximum number of runes allowed in a regexp tree
counting the runes in all the nodes.
Ignoring character classes p.numRunes is always less than the length of the regexp.
Character classes can make it much larger: each \pL adds 1292 runes.
128 MB is enough for 32M runes, which is over 26k \pL instances.
Note that repetitions do not make copies of the rune slices,
so \pL{1000} is only one rune slice, not 1000.
We could keep a cache of character classes we've seen,
so that all the \pL we see use the same rune list,
but that doesn't remove the problem entirely:
consider something like [\pL01234][\pL01235][\pL01236]...[\pL^&*()].
And because the Rune slice is exposed directly in the Regexp,
there is not an opportunity to change the representation to allow
partial sharing between different character classes.
So the limit is the best we can do.

nodes.DocComment:

Fields.Name: numRunes
Fields.DocComment: number of runes in char classes

Fields.Name: height
Fields.DocComment: regexp height, for height limit check

Fields.Name: size
Fields.DocComment: regexp compiled size, for size limit check

nodes.Name: push
nodes.DocComment: push pushes the regexp re onto the parse stack and returns the regexp.

Else.Name: if
Else.RawSource: re.Op == OpCharClass && len(re.Rune) == 4 && re.Rune[0] == re.Rune[1] && re.Rune[2] == re.Rune[3] && unicode.SimpleFold(re.Rune[0]) == re.Rune[2] && unicode.SimpleFold(re.Rune[2]) == re.Rune[0] || re.Op == OpCharClass && len(re.Rune) == 2 && re.Rune[0]+1 == re.Rune[1] && unicode.SimpleFold(re.Rune[0]) == re.Rune[1] && unicode.SimpleFold(re.Rune[1]) == re.Rune[0]

nodes.Name: maybeConcat
nodes.DocComment:
maybeConcat implements incremental concatenation
of literal runes into string nodes. The parser calls this
before each push, so only the top fragment of the stack
might need processing. Since this is called before a push,
the topmost literal is no longer subject to operators like *
(Otherwise ab* would turn into (ab)*.)
If r >= 0 and there's a node left over, maybeConcat uses it
to push r with the given flags.
maybeConcat reports whether r was pushed.

Children.Name: if
Children.RawSource: re1.Op != OpLiteral || re2.Op != OpLiteral || re1.Flags&FoldCase != re2.Flags&FoldCase

nodes.Name: literal
nodes.DocComment: literal pushes a literal regexp for the rune r on the stack.

nodes.Name: minFoldRune
nodes.DocComment: minFoldRune returns the minimum rune fold-equivalent to r.

nodes.Name: op
nodes.DocComment:
op pushes a regexp with the given op onto the stack
and returns that regexp.

nodes.Name: repeat
nodes.DocComment:
repeat replaces the top stack element with itself repeated according to op, min, max.
before is the regexp suffix starting at the repetition operator.
after is the regexp suffix following after the repetition operator.
repeat returns an updated 'after' and an error, if any.

nodes.Name: repeatIsValid
nodes.DocComment:
repeatIsValid reports whether the repetition re is valid.
Valid means that the combination of the top-level repetition
and any inner repetitions does not exceed n copies of the
innermost thing.
This function rewalks the regexp tree and is called for every repetition,
so we have to worry about inducing quadratic behavior in the parser.
We avoid this by only calling repeatIsValid when min or max >= 2.
In that case the depth of any >= 2 nesting can only get to 9 without
triggering a parse error, so each subtree can only be rewalked 9 times.

nodes.Name: concat
nodes.DocComment: concat replaces the top of the stack (above the topmost '|' or '(') with its concatenation.

nodes.Name: alternate
nodes.DocComment: alternate replaces the top of the stack (above the topmost '(') with its alternation.

nodes.Name: cleanAlt
nodes.DocComment: cleanAlt cleans re for eventual inclusion in an alternation.

Children.Name: if
Children.RawSource: len(re.Rune) == 4 && re.Rune[0] == 0 && re.Rune[1] == '\n'-1 && re.Rune[2] == '\n'+1 && re.Rune[3] == unicode.MaxRune

nodes.Name: collapse
nodes.DocComment:
collapse returns the result of applying op to sub.
If sub contains op nodes, they all get hoisted up
so that there is never a concat of a concat or an
alternate of an alternate.

nodes.Name: factor
nodes.DocComment:
factor factors common prefixes from the alternation list sub.
It returns a replacement list that reuses the same storage and
frees (passes to p.reuse) any removed *Regexps.

For example,

	ABC|ABD|AEF|BCX|BCY

simplifies by literal prefix extraction to

	A(B(C|D)|EF)|BC(X|Y)

which simplifies by character class introduction to

	A(B[CD]|EF)|BC[XY]

Children.Name: for
Children.RawSource: same < len(str) && same < len(istr) && str[same] == istr[same]

Children.Name: if
Children.RawSource: first != nil && first.Equal(ifirst) && (isCharClass(first) || (first.Op == OpRepeat && first.Min == first.Max && isCharClass(first.Sub[0])))

Children.Name: if
Children.RawSource: sub[max].Op < sub[j].Op || sub[max].Op == sub[j].Op && len(sub[max].Rune) < len(sub[j].Rune)

Children.Name: if
Children.RawSource: i+1 < len(sub) && sub[i].Op == OpEmptyMatch && sub[i+1].Op == OpEmptyMatch

nodes.Name: leadingString
nodes.DocComment:
leadingString returns the leading literal string that re begins with.
The string refers to storage in re or its children.

nodes.Name: removeLeadingString
nodes.DocComment:
removeLeadingString removes the first n leading runes
from the beginning of re. It returns the replacement for re.

nodes.Name: leadingRegexp
nodes.DocComment:
leadingRegexp returns the leading regexp that re begins with.
The regexp refers to storage in re or its children.

nodes.Name: removeLeadingRegexp
nodes.DocComment:
removeLeadingRegexp removes the leading regexp in re.
It returns the replacement for re.
If reuse is true, it passes the removed regexp (if no longer needed) to p.reuse.

nodes.Name: Parse
nodes.DocComment:
Parse parses a regular expression string s, controlled by the specified
Flags, and returns a regular expression parse tree. The syntax is
described in the top-level comment.

Children.Name: if
Children.RawSource: min < 0 || min > 1000 || max > 1000 || max >= 0 && min > max

nodes.Name: parseRepeat
nodes.DocComment:
parseRepeat parses {min} (max=min) or {min,} (max=-1) or {min,max}.
If s is not of that form, it returns ok == false.
If s has the right form but the values are too big, it returns min == -1, ok == true.

nodes.Name: parsePerlFlags
nodes.DocComment:
parsePerlFlags parses a Perl flag setting or non-capturing group or both,
like (?i) or (?: or (?i:.  It removes the prefix from s and updates the parse state.
The caller must have ensured that s begins with "(?".

nodes.Name: isValidCaptureName
nodes.DocComment:
isValidCaptureName reports whether name
is a valid capture name: [A-Za-z0-9_]+.
PCRE limits names to 32 bytes.
Python rejects names starting with digits.
We don't enforce either of those.

nodes.Name: parseInt
nodes.DocComment: parseInt parses a decimal integer.

nodes.Name: isCharClass
nodes.DocComment:
can this be represented as a character class?
single-rune literal string, char class, ., and .|\n.

nodes.Name: matchRune
nodes.DocComment: does re match r?

nodes.Name: parseVerticalBar
nodes.DocComment: parseVerticalBar handles a | in the input.

nodes.Name: mergeCharClass
nodes.DocComment:
mergeCharClass makes dst = dst|src.
The caller must ensure that dst.Op >= src.Op,
to reduce the amount of copying.

nodes.Name: swapVerticalBar
nodes.DocComment:
If the top of the stack is an element followed by an opVerticalBar
swapVerticalBar swaps the two and returns true.
Otherwise it returns false.

nodes.Name: parseRightParen
nodes.DocComment: parseRightParen handles a ) in the input.

nodes.Name: parseEscape
nodes.DocComment:
parseEscape parses an escape sequence at the beginning of s
and returns the rune.

nodes.Name: parseClassChar
nodes.DocComment:
parseClassChar parses a character class character at the beginning of s
and returns it.

nodes.Name: parsePerlClassEscape
nodes.DocComment:
parsePerlClassEscape parses a leading Perl character class escape like \d
from the beginning of s. If one is present, it appends the characters to r
and returns the new slice r and the remainder of the string.

nodes.Name: parseNamedClass
nodes.DocComment:
parseNamedClass parses a leading POSIX named character class like [:alnum:]
from the beginning of s. If one is present, it appends the characters to r
and returns the new slice r and the remainder of the string.

nodes.Name: anyTable
nodes.ValueLiteral: &unicode.RangeTable{R16: []unicode.Range16{{Lo: 0, Hi: 1<<16 - 1, Stride: 1}}, R32: []unicode.Range32{{Lo: 1 << 16, Hi: unicode.MaxRune, Stride: 1}}}

nodes.Name: asciiFoldTable
nodes.ValueLiteral: &unicode.RangeTable{R16: []unicode.Range16{{Lo: 0, Hi: 0x7F, Stride: 1}, {Lo: 0x017F, Hi: 0x017F, Stride: 1}, {Lo: 0x212A, Hi: 0x212A, Stride: 1}}}

nodes.Name: categoryAliases
nodes.DocComment:
categoryAliases is a lazily constructed copy of unicode.CategoryAliases
but with the keys passed through canonicalName, to support inexact matches.

nodes.Name: initCategoryAliases
nodes.DocComment: initCategoryAliases initializes categoryAliases by canonicalizing unicode.CategoryAliases.

nodes.Name: canonicalName
nodes.DocComment:
canonicalName returns the canonical lookup string for name.
The canonical name has a leading uppercase letter and then lowercase letters,
and it omits all underscores, spaces, and hyphens.
(We could have used all lowercase, but this way most package unicode
map keys are already canonical.)

nodes.Name: unicodeTable
nodes.DocComment:
unicodeTable returns the unicode.RangeTable identified by name
and the table of additional fold-equivalent code points.
If sign < 0, the result should be inverted.

nodes.Name: parseUnicodeClass
parseClass
nodes.DocComment:
parseClass parses a character class at the beginning of s
and pushes it onto the parse stack.

nodes.Name: cleanClass
nodes.DocComment:
cleanClass sorts the ranges (pairs of elements of r),
merges them, and eliminates duplicates.

nodes.Name: inCharClass
nodes.DocComment:
inCharClass reports whether r is in the class.
It assumes the class has been cleaned by cleanClass.

nodes.Name: appendLiteral
nodes.DocComment: appendLiteral returns the result of appending the literal x to the class r.

nodes.Name: appendRange
nodes.DocComment: appendRange returns the result of appending the range lo-hi to the class r.

nodes.Name: appendFoldedRange
nodes.DocComment:
appendFoldedRange returns the result of appending the range lo-hi
and its case folding-equivalent runes to the class r.

nodes.Name: appendClass
nodes.DocComment:
appendClass returns the result of appending the class x to the class r.
It assume x is clean.

nodes.Name: appendFoldedClass
nodes.DocComment: appendFoldedClass returns the result of appending the case folding of the class x to the class r.

nodes.Name: appendNegatedClass
nodes.DocComment:
appendNegatedClass returns the result of appending the negation of the class x to the class r.
It assumes x is clean.

nodes.Name: appendTable
nodes.DocComment: appendTable returns the result of appending x to the class r.

nodes.Name: appendNegatedTable
nodes.DocComment: appendNegatedTable returns the result of appending the negation of x to the class r.

nodes.Name: negateClass
nodes.DocComment:
negateClass overwrites r and returns r's negation.
It assumes the class r is already clean.

nodes.Name: ranges
nodes.DocComment:
ranges implements sort.Interface on a []rune.
The choice of receiver type definition is strange
but avoids an allocation since we already have
a *[]rune.
